Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of the quadratic equation $x^{2} \sin \theta-x(\sin \theta \cos \theta+1)+\cos \theta=0\left(0  < \theta < 45^{\circ}\right),$ and

$\alpha < \beta .$ Then $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\left(\alpha^{n}+\frac{(-1)^{n}}{\beta^{n}}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$x^{2} \sin \theta-x(\sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta+1)+\cos \theta=0$.

$x^{2} \sin \theta-x \sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta-x+\cos \theta=0$x \sin \theta(x-\cos \theta)-1(x-\cos \theta)=0$(x-\cos \theta)(x \sin \theta-1)=0$\therefore x=\cos \theta, \operatorname{cosec} \theta, \theta \in\left(0,45^{\circ}\right)$\therefore \alpha=\cos \theta, \beta=\operatorname{cosec} \theta$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \alpha^{n}=1+\cos \theta+\cos ^{2} \theta+\ldots \infty=\frac{1}{1-\cos \theta}$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n}}{\beta^{n}}=1-\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosec} \theta}+\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosec}^{2} \theta}-\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosec}^{3} \theta}+\ldots \infty$=1-\sin \theta+\sin ^{2} \theta-\sin ^{3} \theta+\ldots \infty$=\frac{1}{1+\sin \theta}$\therefore \quad \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\left(\alpha^{n}+\frac{(-1)^{n}}{\beta^{n}}\right)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \alpha^{n}+\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n}}{\beta^{n}}$=\frac{1}{1-\cos \theta}+\frac{1}{1+\sin \theta} .$

questions.q: If one real root of the quadratic equation $81 x^{2}+k x+256=0$ is cube of the other root, then a value of $\mathrm{k}$ is :
questions.solution:
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of the equation, $81 x^{2}+k x+256=0$

Given $(\alpha)^{\frac{1}{3}}=\beta \Rightarrow \alpha=\beta^{3}$\because \quad$ Product of the roots $=\frac{256}{81}$\therefore \quad(\alpha)(\beta)=\frac{256}{81}$\Rightarrow \quad \beta^{4}=\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)^{4} \Rightarrow \beta=\frac{4}{3} \Rightarrow \alpha=\frac{64}{27}$\because$ Sum of the roots $=-\frac{k}{81}$\therefore \quad \alpha+\beta=-\frac{k}{81} \Rightarrow \frac{4}{3}+\frac{64}{27}=-\frac{k}{81}$\Rightarrow \quad k=-300$

${f}^{′}\left(\lambda\right) = 2\lambda - 4 = 0${$ for the minimum value of $f\left(\lambda\right) }$

As ${f}^{''} ( \lambda ) = 2 > 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 2$

questions.solution:
Let the two roots of ${x}^{2} + 2x + 2 = 0$ be $\alpha$ and $\beta$

$⇒ \alpha, \beta = \dfrac{- 2 \pm \sqrt{4 - 8}}{2} = - 1 \pm i$

$⇒ \alpha, \beta = \sqrt{2}\left(\dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}} \pm i\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$

$= \sqrt{2}\left(cos\dfrac{3\pi}{4} \pm isin\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)$

$⇒ {\alpha}^{15} + {\beta}^{15} = {\left[\sqrt{2}\left(cos\dfrac{3\pi}{4} + isin\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)\right]}^{15} + {\left[\sqrt{2}\left(cos\dfrac{3\pi}{4} - isin\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)\right]}^{15}$

$⇒ {\alpha}^{15} + {\beta}^{15} = 2\dfrac{15}{2}\left[\left(cos\dfrac{45\pi}{4} + isin\dfrac{45\pi}{4}\right) + \left(cos\dfrac{45\pi}{4} - isin\dfrac{45\pi}{4}\right)\right]$

$⇒ {\alpha}^{15} + {\beta}^{15} = 2.2\dfrac{15}{2} . cos\dfrac{45\pi}{4} = 2\dfrac{17}{2} . cos\dfrac{5\pi}{4} = - 2\dfrac{17}{2} . \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ {\alpha}^{15} + {\beta}^{15} = - 256$

questions.q: If $\lambda \in R$ is such that the sum of the cubes of the roots of the equation ${x}^{2} + \left(2 - \lambda\right)x + \left(10 - \lambda\right) = 0$ is minimum, then the magnitude of the difference of the roots of this equation is :
questions.solution:
${x}^{2} + \left(2 - \lambda\right)x + \left(10 - \lambda\right) = 0$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta = \lambda - 2 \text{$ and $} \alpha\beta = 10 - \lambda . . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Let roots are $\alphaand\beta$.

$⇒ {\alpha}^{3} + {\beta}^{3} = {\left(\alpha + \beta\right)}^{3} - 3\alpha\beta ( \alpha + \beta )$

$= {\left(\lambda - 2\right)}^{3} - 3\left(10 - \lambda\right) ( \lambda - 2 )$

$= {\lambda}^{3} - {6\lambda}^{2} + 12\lambda - 8 - 3 ( 10\lambda - {\lambda}^{2} - 20 + 2\lambda )$

$= {\lambda}^{3} - {3\lambda}^{2} - 24\lambda + 52$

$\dfrac{dz}{d\lambda} = 3{\lambda}^{2} - 6\lambda - 24 = 3\left({\lambda}^{2} - 2\lambda - 8\right)$ (where, $z = {\alpha}^{3} + {\beta}^{3}$)

For maximum and critical points, derivative must be zero.

$⇒ {\lambda}^{2} - 2\lambda - 8 = 0$

$⇒ \left(\lambda - 4\right)\left(\lambda + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = - 2,4$

Now, $\dfrac{{d}^{2}z}{d{\lambda}^{2}} = 6\lambda - 6$

For $\left(\lambda = - 2\right), \dfrac{{d}^{2}z}{d{\lambda}^{2}} < 0 ⇒ {\alpha}^{3} + {\beta}^{3}$ is maximum and

For $( \lambda = 4 ) , \dfrac{{d}^{2}z}{d{\lambda}^{2}} > 0 ⇒ {\alpha}^{3} + {\beta}^{3}$ is minimum.

$⇒$Equation will be ${x}^{2} - 2x + 6 = 0$.

Using quadratic formula, we get

$x = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{{\left(- 2\right)}^{2} - 4 \times 1 \times 6}}{2 \times 1} = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{- 20}}{2} = \dfrac{2 \pm 2\sqrt{5}i}{2} = 1 \pm \sqrt{5}i$

Thus, difference of roots is $\left|\alpha - \beta\right| = 2\sqrt{5}$

questions.solution:
Since, $tan ⁡ A$ and $tan ⁡ B$ are roots of the equation $3{x}^{2} - 10x - 25 = 0$.

So, $tan ⁡ A + tan ⁡ B = \dfrac{10}{3}$ and $tan ⁡ A . tan ⁡ B = - \dfrac{25}{3}$

$∴ tan ⁡ \left(A + B\right) = \dfrac{tan ⁡ A + tan ⁡ B}{1 - tan ⁡ A . tan ⁡ B} = \dfrac{\dfrac{10}{3}}{1 + \dfrac{25}{3}} = \dfrac{10}{28} = \dfrac{5}{14}$

So, $sin\left(A + B\right) = \dfrac{\pm 5}{\sqrt{221}} \text{ and } cos\left(A + B\right) = \dfrac{\pm 14}{\sqrt{221}}$

(Note that either both are negative or both positive)

$∴ 3\sin^{2} ⁡ \left(A + B\right) - 10sin ⁡ \left(A + B\right) . cos ⁡ \left(A + B\right) - 25\cos^{2} ⁡ \left(A + B\right)$

$= 3 \times \dfrac{25}{221} - \dfrac{10 \times 5 \times 14}{221} - 25 \times \dfrac{{14}^{2}}{221}$

$= \dfrac{25}{221}\left(3 - 28 - 196\right) = - 25$

$p\left(x\right) = 4{x}^{2} - x + 1$

$p\left(- 2\right) = 16 + 2 + 1 = 19$

questions.q:
If, for a positive integer $n$, the quadratic equation,

$x\left(x + 1\right) + \left(x + 1\right)\left(x + 2\right) + . .. + \left(x + \overset{¯}{n - 1}\right)\left(x + n\right) = 10n$

has two consecutive integral solutions, then $n$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
On simplifying we get the quadratic equations as
$\left(\mathop{\mathop{{x}^{2} + {x}^{2} + . . . + {x}^{2}}_{⏟}}_{n\text{times}}\right) + \left[1 + 3 + 5 + . . . + \left(2n - 1\right)\right]x + \left[1 . 2 + 2 . 3 + . . . + \left(n - 1\right)n\right] = 10n$
$n{x}^{2} + {n}^{2}x + \dfrac{n\left({n}^{2} - 1\right)}{3} = 10n$

${x}^{2} + nx + \dfrac{{n}^{2} - 31}{3} = 0$

Let, $\alpha, \beta$ are the roots of the above equation

$∴ \alpha + \beta = - n, \alpha\beta = \dfrac{{n}^{2} - 31}{3}$

Now, the difference of roots$\left|\alpha - \beta\right| = 1$

$⇒ {\left(\alpha - \beta\right)}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ {\left(\alpha + \beta\right)}^{2} - 4\alpha\beta = 1$

$⇒ {n}^{2} - \dfrac{4}{3}\left({n}^{2} - 31\right) = 1$

$⇒ {n}^{2} = 121$

$⇒ n = 11$

questions.q: If the equations ${x}^{2} + bx - 1 = 0 and {x}^{2} + x + b = 0$ have a common root different from $- 1,$ then $\left|b\right|$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let common root be $x$
${x}^{2} + bx - 1 = 0$ ...$\left(1\right)$

${x}^{2} + x + b = 0$ ...$\left(2\right)$

$\left(1\right) - \left(2\right)$, we get $x = \dfrac{b + 1}{b - 1}$

Put $x$ in Equation $\left(1\right)$, we get

${\left(\dfrac{b + 1}{b - 1}\right)}^{2} + \left(\dfrac{b + 1}{b - 1}\right) + b = 0$

$⇒${\left(b + 1\right)}^{2} + \left(b + 1\right)\left(b - 1\right) + b{\left(b - 1\right)}^{2} = 0$

$⇒${b}^{2} + 1 + 2b + {b}^{2} - 1 + b\left({b}^{2} - 2b + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒$2{b}^{2} + 2b + {b}^{3} - 2{b}^{2} + b = 0$

$⇒  ${b}^{3} + 3b = 0$
$⇒   $b\left({b}^{2} + 3\right) = 0 ⇒ b = 0$ or ${b}^{2} = - 3$

When $b = 0$ then common root $x = - 1$
But the given common root $x \ne - 1$

$∴${b}^{2} = - 3$

$b = \pm \sqrt{3}i$

$\left|b\right| = \sqrt{3}$

questions.q: The equation $\sqrt{3{x}^{2} + x + 5} = x - 3$, where $x ⁡$ is real, has
questions.solution:
$\sqrt{3{x}^{2} + x + 5} = x - 3 . . . \left(1\right)

We know that$ for a quadratic expressiona{x}^{2} + bx + c, a > 0,$ if discriminant i.e. $D = {b}^{2} - 4ac < 0,$ then the quadratic is always positive for all real values of the variable.

Now, consider $3{x}^{2} + x + 5$

We have, discriminant $= {b}^{2} - 4ac = 1 - 4 \times 3 \times 5 < 0$

$∴ 3{x}^{2} + x + 5 > 0, ∀ x \in R$

Squaring \left(1\right),$ we get,

$3{x}^{2} + x + 5 = {\left(x - 3\right)$}^{2}$

$⇒ 3{x}^{2} + x + 5 = {x}^{2} - 6x + 9$

$⇒ 2{x}^{2} + 7x - 4 = 0$

$⇒ $\left(x + 4\right)\left(2x - 1\right)$ = 0$

$⇒ x = - 4,x = $\dfrac{1}{2}$

But $x - 3 < 0$ for $x = - 4, \dfrac{1}{2}$

Hence, the equation has no solution.

questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are roots of the equation, $x^2-4 \sqrt{2} k x+2 e^{4 \ln k}-1=0$ for some $k$, and $\alpha^2+\beta^2=66$, then $\alpha^3+\beta^3$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$x^2-4 \sqrt{2} k x+2 e^{4 \ln k}-1=0$ or, $x^2-4 \sqrt{2} k x+2 k^4-1=0 \alpha+\beta=4 \sqrt{2} k$ and $\alpha \cdot \beta=2 k^4-1$ Squaring both sides, we get

\begin{aligned}
&(\alpha+\beta)^2=(4 \sqrt{2} k)^2 \\
&\Rightarrow \alpha^2+\beta^2+2 \alpha \beta=32 k^2 \\
&66+2 \alpha \beta=32 k^2 \\
&66+2 $\left(2 k^4-1\right)$=32 k^2 \\
&66+4 k^4-2=32 k^2 \\
&\Rightarrow 4 k^4-32 k^2+64=0 \\
&$\text{ or, }$ k^4-8 k^2+16=0 \\
&\Rightarrow $\left(k^2\right)^2$-8 k^2+16=0 \\
&\Rightarrow $\left(k^2-4\right)\left(k^2-4\right)=0 \\
&\Rightarrow k^2=4, k^2=4 \\
&\Rightarrow k=\pm 2
\end{aligned}

Now, $\alpha^3+\beta^3=(\alpha+\beta) $\left(\alpha^2+\beta^2-\alpha \beta\right) 
\therefore \alpha^3+\beta^3=(4 \sqrt{2} k) \left[66-\left(2 k^4-1\right)$\right]

Putting $k=-2,(k=+2$ cannot be taken because it does not satisfy the above equation)
$\therefore \alpha^3+\beta^3=(4 \sqrt{2}(-2))\left[66-2(-2)^4-1\right] \alpha^3+\beta^3=(-8 \sqrt{2})(66-32+1)= (-8 \sqrt{2})(35) \therefore \alpha^3+\beta^3=-280 \sqrt{2}$

questions.solution:
$a{x}^{2} + bx + 1 = 0$ has roots $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha}}, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\beta}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha}} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\beta}} = - \dfrac{b}{a} . . . \left(1\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha}\sqrt{\beta}} = \dfrac{1}{a} . . . \left(2\right)$

$x\left(x + {b}^{3}\right) + \left({a}^{3} - 3abx\right) = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + \left({b}^{3} - 3ab\right)x + {a}^{3} = 0$

Multiply and divide with ${a}^{3}$, we get

$⇒ {x}^{2} + {a}^{3}\left\{\left(\dfrac{{b}^{3}}{{a}^{3}}\right) - 3\dfrac{1}{a}\left(\dfrac{b}{a}\right)\right\}x + {a}^{3} = 0$
From equations $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$,
$⇒ {x}^{2} + {\left(\alpha\beta\right)}^{3 / 2}\left[- \dfrac{{\left({\alpha}^{1 / 2} + {\beta}^{1 / 2}\right)}^{3}}{{\left(\sqrt{\alpha\beta}\right)}^{3}} - 3\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha\beta}}\dfrac{\sqrt{\alpha} + \sqrt{\beta}}{\sqrt{\alpha\beta}}\right]x + {\left(\alpha\beta\right)}^{3 / 2} = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - \left({\alpha}^{3 / 2} + {\beta}^{3 / 2}\right)x + {\alpha}^{3 / 2}{\beta}^{3 / 2} = 0$

Roots are $\alpha\dfrac{3}{2}\text{and}\beta\dfrac{3}{2}$.

$= \dfrac{- 1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 3{a}^{2}}}{- 3} = \dfrac{1 ∓ \sqrt{1 + 3{a}^{2}}}{3}$

$∴ 1 + \sqrt{1 + 3{a}^{2}} < 3$

$∴ 1 + 3{a}^{2} < 4$

$∴ 3{a}^{2} < 3$

questions.q: Let $\alpha \text{and} \beta$ be the roots of equation $p{x}^{2} + qx + r = 0$, $p \ne 0$. If $p, q, r$are in A.P. and $\dfrac{1}{\alpha} + \dfrac{1}{\beta} = 4$, then the value of $\left|\alpha - \beta\right|$ is
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{1}{\alpha} + \dfrac{1}{\beta} = 4$

$\dfrac{\alpha + \beta}{\alpha \beta} = 4$

$∴ \dfrac{- \dfrac{q}{p}}{\dfrac{r}{p}} = 4$

$∴ - \dfrac{q}{r} = 4$

$p, q, r$ are in A.P.

Let $p = a - d; q = a, r = a + d$.

$∴ \dfrac{- \left(a\right)}{a + d} = 4 ⇒ - a = 4a + 4d ⇒ d = \dfrac{- 5a}{4}$

$p = a + \dfrac{5a}{4} = \dfrac{9a}{4}; q = a, r = a - \dfrac{5a}{4} = - \dfrac{a}{4}$

$∴ \dfrac{9}{4}{x}^{2} + \dfrac{4}{4}x - \dfrac{1}{4} = 0$

$∴ 9 {x}^{2} + 4x - 1 = 0$

${\left|\alpha - \beta\right|}^{2} = {\left(\alpha + \beta\right)}^{2} - 4 \alpha \beta$

$= {\left(\dfrac{- 4}{9}\right)}^{2} - 4 \left(- \dfrac{1}{\text{9}}\right)$

$= \dfrac{1 6}{8 1} + \dfrac{4}{9} = \dfrac{5 2}{8 1}$

$∴ \left|\alpha - \beta\right| = \dfrac{2 \sqrt{1 3}}{9}$.

Hence, the correct answer is $\dfrac{2 \sqrt{1 3}}{9}$.

Consider a quadratic equation $a x^2+b x+c=0$, where $2 a+3 b+6 c=0$ and let $g(x)=a \frac{x^3}{3}+b \frac{x^2}{2}+c x$.
Statement 1: The quadratic equation has at least one root in the interval $(0,1)$.
Statement 2: The Rolle's theorem is applicable to function $g(x)$ on the interval $[0,1]$.
options:
Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true.

Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false.

Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is true, Statement 2 is not a correct explanation for Statement 1.

Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is true, , Statement 2 is a correct explanation for Statement 1.
questions.solution:
Let $g(x)=\frac{a x^3}{3}+b \cdot \frac{x^2}{2}+c x$
\mathrmg^{\prime}(x)=a x²+b x+c

Given: $a x^2+b x+c=0 and 2 a+3 b+6 c=0$
Statement-2:
(i) g(0)=0 and $g(1) \begin{aligned}$& =$\frac{a}{3}+\frac{b}{2}+$c=$\frac{2 a+3 b+6 c}{6}$\\
& =$\frac{0}{6}=$0 \\
& \Rightarrow g(0)=g(1)
\end{aligned}

(ii) $g$ is continuous on $[0,1]$ and differentiable on $(0,1)\therefore$ By Rolle's theorem $\exists k \in(0,1)$ such that $g^{\prime}(k)=0$
This holds the statement 2. Also, from statement-2, we can say $a x^2+b x+c=0$ has at least one root in $(0,1)$.
Thus statement-1 and 2 both are true and statement-2 is a correct explanation for statement-1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $2 a+3 b+6 c=0(a, b, c \in R)$ then the quadratic equation $a x^2+b x+c=0$ has
options:
at least one root in [0, 1]

at least one root in [2, 3]

at least one root in [4, 5]

none of these
questions.solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{a x^3}{3}+\frac{b x^2}{2}+c x \Rightarrow f(0)=0$ and $f(1)=\frac{a}{3}+\frac{b}{2}+c=\frac{2 a+3 b+6 c}{6}=0$
Also $f(x)$ is continuous and differentiable in $[0,1] and \left[0,1]\right.$. So by Rolle's theorem, $f^{\prime}(x)=0$. i.e. $a x^2+b x+c=0$ has at least one root in $[0,1]$
